css-specificity.promptSeed:
Calculate and compare CSS selector specificity vectors:

### `specificity(selector: string): [ids: number, classes: number, elements: number]`
- Parses a single complex selector string (no top-level commas).
- Returns a 3-tuple `[ids, classes, elements]`:
  - **IDs (`ids`)**: counts `#id` selectors.
  - **Classes (`classes`)**: counts `.class`, `[attribute]` selectors, and `:pseudo-class` selectors.
  - **Elements (`elements`)**: counts type/tag selectors and `::pseudo-element` selectors.
- **Rules & Modifiers**:
  - Combinators (` `, `>`, `+`, `~`) and the universal selector `*` add nothing `[0, 0, 0]`.
  - `:where(X)` adds nothing `[0, 0, 0]`.
  - `:not(X)` adds the specificity of its inner argument `X` (the `:not` pseudo-class itself contributes 0).

### `compareSpecificity(a: string, b: string): 1 | -1 | 0`
- Compares the specificity of two selector strings `a` and `b` by comparing `ids`, then `classes`, then `elements`.
- Returns `1` if selector `a` is more specific than `b`.
- Returns `-1` if selector `b` is more specific than `a`.
- Returns `0` if they have identical specificity.

client-side-router.promptSeed:
Implement an in-memory client-side router with path parameters and query string parsing:

### `matchRoute(pattern: string, pathname: string): Record<string, string> | null`
- Matches a pathname against a pattern and extracts route parameters (supports `:param` and `*` wildcard).

### `createRouter(routes: Array<{ pattern: string; name: string }>, initialPath?: string): Router`
- `routes` is an array of route definitions: `[{ pattern: '/users/:id', name: 'user' }, ...]`.
- Initialized with `initialPath` (defaults to `'/'`).

#### Route Resolution
- Matches paths against route patterns:
  - Segments starting with `':name'` capture dynamic parameters into `params: { name: value }`.
  - Empty segments (leading, trailing, and duplicate slashes) are ignored.
  - Query parameters (e.g. `'?q=hi&page=2'`) are parsed into `query: { q: 'hi', page: '2' }`.
  - If no route matches, resolves to `{ path, name: null, params: {}, query }`.

#### Router API
- **`current()`**: Returns the currently active resolved route object `{ path, name, params, query }`.
- **`navigate(path)`**: Pushes `path` onto history, drops forward history, updates the current route, and notifies listeners.
- **`back()`**: Moves one step back in history (if possible) and notifies listeners.
- **`forward()`**: Moves one step forward in history (if possible) and notifies listeners.
- **`subscribe(listener)`**: Subscribes `listener(route)` to navigation events and returns an unsubscribe function.

storage-ttl-wrapper.promptSeed:
Wrap a `localStorage`-like backend with namespacing and TTL (Time-To-Live) expiration:

### `createStorage(backend: Storage, options?: { prefix?: string; now?: () => number }): StorageWrapper`
- Wraps `backend` supporting `getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`, `key(i)`, and `length`.
- Options:
  - `prefix`: string namespace prepended to all backend keys (defaults to `'app:'`).
  - `now`: timestamp generator function (defaults to `Date.now`).

#### Storage Methods
- **`set(key, value, { ttlMs } = {})`**:
  - Stores value as JSON with expiration timestamp: `{ v: value, e: ttlMs ? now() + ttlMs : null }`.
  - Returns `true` on success, or `false` if `backend.setItem` throws (e.g. storage quota exceeded).
- **`get(key, fallback = null)`**:
  - Reads stored entry. Returns `fallback` if the key is missing.
  - If the item has expired (`now() >= entry.e`) or contains corrupt JSON, removes it from storage and returns `fallback`.
  - Otherwise returns the stored value `entry.v`.
- **`remove(key)`**:
  - Removes the namespaced key from `backend`.
- **`keys()`**:
  - Returns an array of keys belonging to this namespace, stripping the prefix.
- **`clear()`**:
  - Removes all keys belonging to this namespace without touching other keys in `backend`.

vnode-to-dom.promptSeed:
Implement a lightweight virtual DOM to real DOM compiler and renderer:

### createDom(vnode: VNode): Node
- Converts a virtual node tree into real DOM nodes.
- **Primitives**:
  - `string` or `number`: creates a safe text node via `document.createTextNode(String(vnode))` (never parsed as HTML).
  - `null`, `undefined`, or `boolean`: returns an empty text node (`document.createTextNode('')`).
- **Elements**:
  - Creates the element with `document.createElement(vnode.type)`.
  - **Props Handling**:
    - `className`: sets the `'class'` attribute.
    - `style`: copies style properties onto `el.style` (`Object.assign(el.style, value)`).
    - Event handlers (e.g. `onClick`, `onInput`): attaches listener via `el.addEventListener(event, fn)`.
    - `true`: sets attribute to empty string `''`.
    - `false`, `null`, or `undefined`: attribute is omitted.
    - Other values: calls `el.setAttribute(key, String(value))`.
  - **Children**:
    - Recursively flattens and renders `vnode.children || []` (handles arbitrarily nested arrays).

### render(vnode: VNode, container: HTMLElement): void
- Compiles `vnode` via `createDom(vnode)` and replaces the container's contents using `container.replaceChildren(...)`.

parse-path-params.promptSeed:
Extract named dynamic route parameters from a URL path:

### `parsePath(pattern: string, path: string): Record<string, string> | null`
- Parses dynamic path parameters defined by `:param` segments in `pattern`.
- Example: `parsePath('/users/:id/posts/:postId', '/users/7/posts/42')` returns `{ id: '7', postId: '42' }`.

#### Matching Rules
- Normalizes paths: ignores trailing slashes and discards any query string (`?query`) or hash fragment (`#hash`).
- Compares segment by segment:
  - Dynamic segments (starting with `':'`) extract their corresponding value into the params object.
  - Static segments must match identically.
- Returns `null` if the segment count differs or if any static segment fails to match.

parse-style-string.promptSeed:
Convert between CSS inline style strings and JavaScript style objects:

### parseStyle(text: string): Record<string, string>
- Parses an inline CSS style declaration string (e.g. `'color: red; margin-top: 4px;'`).
- Returns a camelCased style object: `{ color: 'red', marginTop: '4px' }`.
- Rules:
  - Splits declarations on `';'` and ignores empty segments.
  - Splits each declaration at the **first colon only** (values may contain colons, such as in `url(...)`).
  - Trims leading and trailing whitespace from both property names and values.
  - Converts kebab-case property names to camelCase (`margin-top` -> `marginTop`).
    - Helper expression: `name.replace(/-([a-z])/g, (_, c) => c.toUpperCase())`

### styleToString(obj: Record<string, string | number>): string
- Converts a style object back into a CSS inline style string.
- Converts camelCase keys to kebab-case (e.g. `marginTop` -> `margin-top`).
  - Helper expression: `name.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => '-' + c.toLowerCase())`
- Formats each property as `property: value;`.
- Joins multiple declarations separated by a single space (e.g. `'color: red; margin-top: 4px;'`).

safe-json-storage.promptSeed:
Safe JSON parsing and browser storage read/write utilities:

### `safeParse<T>(text: unknown, fallback: T): T`
- Returns the parsed JSON or `fallback` when text is not valid JSON (or not a string).

### `safeGet<T>(storage: { getItem(key: string): string | null }, key: string, fallback: T): T`
- Reads `storage.getItem(key)` (a localStorage-like object with `getItem` and `setItem`) and returns the parsed value or `fallback` when the key is missing or the stored text is corrupt.

### `safeSet(storage: { setItem(key: string, value: string): void }, key: string, value: unknown): boolean`
- Stringifies `value` with `JSON.stringify` and stores the JSON string with `storage.setItem(key, jsonString)`, returning `true`, or `false` if `storage.setItem` throws.

next-route-matcher.promptSeed:
Implement Next.js-style route pattern matching:

### `matchRoute(pattern: string, pathname: string): { params: Record<string, string | string[]> } | null`

Segment rules:
1. Static segments: exact string match (e.g. `/posts/latest`).
2. Single dynamic parameter: `[param]` matches exactly one non-empty path segment. Returns `{ [param]: segmentString }`.
3. Catch-all parameter: `[...slug]` matches one or more path segments. Returns `{ [slug]: [segment1, segment2, ...] }`. Fails (returns `null`) if zero segments are provided.
4. Optional catch-all parameter: `[[...slug]]` matches zero or more path segments. Returns `{ [slug]: [segment1, ...] }` or `{ [slug]: [] }` if no segments match.

Return value:
- Returns `{ params: Record<string, string | string[]> }` if `pathname` matches `pattern`.
- Returns `null` if `pathname` does not match the pattern.
- Leading and trailing slashes should be normalized.

#### Useful Patterns
- Optional catch-all: `segment.match(/^\[\[\.\.\.([^\]]+)\]\]$/)`
- Catch-all: `segment.match(/^\[\.\.\.([^\]]+)\]$/)`
- Dynamic parameter: `segment.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]$/)`

cookie-parse-serialize.promptSeed:
Implement HTTP cookie parsing and serialization utilities:

### `parseCookies(header: string | null | undefined): Record<string, string>`
- Parses a `Cookie` request header or `document.cookie` string (e.g. `'a=1; b=hello%20world'`).
- Returns an object mapping cookie names to decoded values:
  - Splits segments on `';'` and skips empty segments.
  - Splits each segment at the **first `'='` only** (cookie values may contain equal signs).
  - Trims both name and value.
  - Decodes values with `decodeURIComponent` (if decoding throws, preserves the raw text).
  - Preserves the **first** occurrence if a cookie name is duplicated.

### `serializeCookie(name: string, value: string, options?: CookieOptions): string`
- Generates a `Set-Cookie` header string: `name=encodeURIComponent(value)`.
- **Validation**:
  - Throws `TypeError('Invalid cookie name')` if `name` is empty or contains `'='`, `';'`, `','`, or whitespace.
  - If `options.sameSite` is provided, accepts case-insensitive `'strict'`, `'lax'`, or `'none'`. Throws `TypeError('Invalid SameSite value')` for any other value.
- **Attributes Ordering** (appends provided attributes in this exact order):
  1. `; Max-Age=<n>` (integer from `options.maxAge`; note: `0` must be emitted).
  2. `; Expires=<utc string>` (`options.expires.toUTCString()`).
  3. `; Domain=<domain>`.
  4. `; Path=<path>`.
  5. `; Secure` (if `options.secure === true`).
  6. `; HttpOnly` (if `options.httpOnly === true`).
  7. `; SameSite=<Strict|Lax|None>` (capitalized: `'Strict'`, `'Lax'`, or `'None'`).

copy-to-clipboard.promptSeed:
Write async text copying utility with HTML5 Clipboard API and DOM textarea fallback:

### `copyToClipboard(text: string, env?: { navigator?: any; document?: any }): Promise<boolean>`

`env` holds the browser objects to use (`{ navigator, document }`) so they can be replaced in tests: use the browser global only when that key is missing from `env`, and treat an explicit `null` or `undefined` value as "not available".

1. **Async Clipboard API**: If `env.navigator.clipboard.writeText` exists, `await` it and resolve `true`. If it is missing or its promise rejects, fall back.
2. **Fallback**: Create a `<textarea>` with `document.createElement`, set its `value` to the text, mark it `readonly`, and move it off screen (`style.position = 'fixed'`, `style.left = '-9999px'`). Append it to `document.body`, call `select()` on it, then run `document.execCommand('copy')` and resolve with its boolean result.
3. **Cleanup**: Always remove the `<textarea>` from `document.body` afterwards, even when `execCommand` throws (a throw resolves `false`). If there is no document, resolve `false`.

keyboard-shortcut-matcher.promptSeed:
Write three utility functions for managing and matching keyboard shortcuts: `parseShortcut`, `matchesShortcut`, and `findShortcut`.

### parseShortcut(text: string): ParsedShortcut
- Parses a shortcut string (e.g. `'Ctrl+Shift+K'`) into `{ key, ctrl, meta, alt, shift, mod }`.
- Split tokens on `'+'`, trim whitespace, and normalize case-insensitively.
- The returned non-modifier `key` is lowercased.
- Maps modifier and key aliases:
  - `control` $\rightarrow$ `ctrl`
  - `cmd` and `command` $\rightarrow$ `meta`
  - `option` $\rightarrow$ `alt`
  - `esc` $\rightarrow$ `escape`
  - `return` $\rightarrow$ `enter`
  - `space` $\rightarrow$ `' '`
  - `'mod'` is recorded in its own boolean flag.

### matchesShortcut(event: KeyEventLike, shortcut: string | ParsedShortcut, isMac?: boolean): boolean
- Takes an event-like object `{ key, ctrlKey, metaKey, altKey, shiftKey }` and a parsed shortcut (or string).
- Returns `true` only when the primary `key` matches (case-insensitive) **AND** all modifier flags match exactly (any missing or extra modifier fails the match).
- When `shortcut.mod` is set: evaluates as `metaKey` on Mac (`isMac: true`) and `ctrlKey` on non-Mac platforms (`isMac: false`).

### findShortcut(event: KeyEventLike, bindings: Record<string, string | ParsedShortcut>, isMac?: boolean): string | null
- Takes an event object and a dictionary `bindings` of `{ [actionName]: shortcutStringOrObject }`.
- Returns the action name of the first matching binding, or `null` if none match.

drop-index-from-pointer.promptSeed:
Write the logic behind a drag-sortable list:

### dropIndex(pointerY: number, rects: Rect[]): number
- Takes the pointer's vertical position and an array of `{ top, height }` rectangles (one per item, top to bottom).
- Returns the insertion index `0...rects.length`: the position of the first item whose vertical midpoint is BELOW the pointer (a pointer exactly on a midpoint counts as past it), or `rects.length` when the pointer is below every midpoint.

### moveItem<T>(list: T[], from: number, to: number): T[]
- Returns a NEW array with the item at index `from` moved so that it sits in the gap `to` of the ORIGINAL list (gap 0 is before the first item, gap `list.length` after the last one).
- Moving an item into its own gap (`to === from` or `to === from + 1`) returns an unchanged copy. Never mutate the input.

### reorderOnDrop<T>(list: T[], from: number, pointerY: number, rects: Rect[]): T[]
- Combines `dropIndex` and `moveItem`: calculates the target gap with `dropIndex(pointerY, rects)` and moves the item.

raf-throttle.promptSeed:
Implement requestAnimationFrame-based throttling for high-frequency events:

### rafThrottle<TArgs extends unknown[]>(fn: (...args: TArgs) => void, raf?: (cb: (time: number) => void) => number, caf?: (handle: number) => void): ThrottledFunction<TArgs>
- Returns a throttled function that invokes `fn` at most once per animation frame.
- Defaults to window `requestAnimationFrame` and `cancelAnimationFrame` (can be dependency-injected in tests).

#### Throttling Mechanics
- Remembers the latest arguments passed across invocations.
- The first invocation schedules a frame via `raf(...)`. Subsequent calls before that frame fires simply replace the arguments.
- When the frame executes:
  - Invokes `fn` once with the latest arguments.
  - Clears the active frame ID so subsequent calls (including calls inside `fn`) can schedule a new frame.

#### Cancellation
- The returned throttled function exposes a `.cancel()` method:
  - If a frame is pending, cancels it via `caf(frameId)` and clears the pending state.
  - Does nothing (and does not call `caf`) if no frame is currently pending.

### createSequenceMatcher(bindings: Record<string, string>, timeoutMs?: number): (key: string, now: number) => string | null
Write `createSequenceMatcher(bindings, timeoutMs = 1000)` for GitHub / Vim-style multi-key sequences (e.g. `'g i'`):

- **Parameters**:
  - `bindings`: Maps space-separated key sequences to action names (e.g. `{ 'g i': 'goIssues', 'g p': 'goPulls', '?': 'help' }`). No sequence is a prefix of another.
  - `timeoutMs`: Maximum duration allowed between consecutive key presses (defaults to `1000` ms).
- **Returned Function**: Returns `press(key, now)` where `now` is a timestamp in milliseconds. Returns the matched action name when the key completes a sequence, and `null` otherwise.
- **Sequence Rules**:
  1. **Timeout**: If more than `timeoutMs` has elapsed since the previous key press (exactly `timeoutMs` is still valid), the pending sequence is reset first. The timeout is measured from the previous key press, not from sequence start.
  2. **Advance**: A key that matches the expected next token in the sequence advances the pending buffer.
  3. **Mismatch & Restart**: A key that breaks the current sequence resets the buffer, but can immediately act as the first key of a new sequence (e.g. `'g'`, `'g'`, `'i'` successfully completes `'g i'`).
  4. **Post-Match**: Upon completing a match, the buffer resets fresh.

Implement element container queries using `ResizeObserver`:

### observeBreakpoint(element: Element, breakpoints: Record<string, number>, onChange: (name: string | null) => void, RO?: ResizeObserverConstructorLike): () => void
- Observes the content width of `element` and triggers `onChange(name)` when its matching container breakpoint changes.
- `breakpoints` maps breakpoint names to minimum width thresholds in any key order (e.g. `{ sm: 0, md: 600, lg: 1000 }`).

#### Breakpoint Matching
- Reads `entry.contentRect.width` from the observer entries.
- The active breakpoint is the one with the **largest minimum threshold** that is less than or equal to the element's width (boundary values belong to that breakpoint).
- If the width is below all thresholds, the active breakpoint is `null`.

#### Notification & Lifecycle
- Calls `onChange(name)` on the initial measurement.
- Afterwards, calls `onChange(name)` **only** when the resolved breakpoint changes (including transitions to or from `null`).
- Returns a cleanup function `() => void` that disconnects the observer.

### watchForElements(root: Element, selector: string, onFound: (element: Element) => void, MO?: MutationObserverConstructorLike): () => void
Write `watchForElements(root, selector, onFound, MO = MutationObserver)`:

- **Initial Discovery**: Calls `onFound(element)` for all matching elements already present in `root` in document order (`root.querySelectorAll(selector)`).
- **Mutation Observation**:

    - Report any matching descendants found via `node.querySelectorAll(selector)`.
- **Deduplication**: Each unique element is reported at most once, even if delivered across multiple mutation records.
- **Cleanup**: Returns a `stop()` function that disconnects the observer.

mini-history-router.promptSeed:
Write a tiny client-side router built on the HTML5 History API:

### createRouter(routes: Array<{ name: string; path: string }>, win = window): Router:
- `routes` is an ordered list of route definitions like `[{ name: 'user', path: '/users/:id' }]`.
- Starts from `win.location.pathname` and listens for `'popstate'` on `win` (browser back/forward) by resolving `win.location.pathname` again.

#### Pattern Matching & Route Resolution
- A segment starting with `':'` captures a named parameter (decoded with `decodeURIComponent`).
- Every other segment must match exactly.
- The number of segments must be equal; empty segments (leading, trailing, and double slashes) are ignored.
- The first matching route in the list wins.
- A path with no match resolves to `name: null` with `{ name: null, params: {}, path }`.
- A resolved route object is `{ name: string | null, params: Record<string, string>, path: string }` where `path` is the path as given.

#### Router Return Object (`Router`)
Returns `{ current(), navigate(path), replace(path), subscribe(fn), destroy() }`:
- **`current(): { name: string | null, params: Record<string, string>, path: string }`**:
  - Returns the current resolved route.
- **`navigate(path: string): void`**:
  - Does nothing when `path` equals the current route's path (`current().path`).
  - Otherwise calls `win.history.pushState(null, '', path)`, updates the route, and notifies subscribers.
- **`replace(path: string): void`**:
  - Calls `win.history.replaceState(null, '', path)`, updates the route, and notifies subscribers (always applies, even if `path` equals the current path).
- **`subscribe(fn: (route: { name: string | null, params: Record<string, string>, path: string }) => void): () => void`**:
  - Calls `fn(route)` on every route change (not called immediately upon subscription).
  - Returns an unsubscribe function.
- **`destroy(): void`**:
  - Removes the `'popstate'` listener from `win` and clears all subscribers.

dom-toggle-active-class.promptSeed:
Implement a foundational DOM utility that binds a click listener to toggle an active class and synchronize aria-expanded:

## Description

### Application Context
When building accessible interactive widgets without a heavy framework (`nav/disclosure.ts`), developers frequently need a clean vanilla DOM helper to bind a trigger button to a target drawer, panel, or menu, toggling an active class while keeping ARIA attributes synchronized. You are implementing a DOM binding controller.

```ts
interface ToggleBindingOptions {
  triggerId: string;
  targetId: string;
  activeClass?: string;
  initialExpanded?: boolean;
}

interface ToggleBindingController {
  isExpanded(): boolean;
  destroy(): void;
}
```

### `bindClassToggle(options: ToggleBindingOptions): ToggleBindingController`

Finds the trigger and target DOM elements by ID, initializes their state, and wires a click listener:

- **Element Lookup & Validation**:
  - Finds the trigger element with `document.getElementById(options.triggerId)` and target element with `document.getElementById(options.targetId)`.
  - If either element is not found in the DOM, throws `new Error('Required element not found')`.
- **Configuration Defaults**:
  - `activeClass`: Defaults to `'active'`.
  - `initialExpanded`: Defaults to `false`.
- **Initial State Setup**:
  - If `initialExpanded` is `true`:
    - Adds `activeClass` to `target.classList`.
    - Sets `trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')`.
  - If `initialExpanded` is `false`:
    - Removes `activeClass` from `target.classList`.
    - Sets `trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')`.
- **Event Handling**:
  - Listens for `'click'` events on the trigger element.
  - On click:
    - Toggles `activeClass` on `target.classList`.
    - Reads whether `target.classList.contains(activeClass)`.
    - Updates `trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(isNowActive))`.
- **Return Controller**:
  - Returns an object implementing `ToggleBindingController`:
    - **`isExpanded(): boolean`**: Returns `target.classList.contains(activeClass)`.
    - **`destroy(): void`**: Removes the `'click'` event listener from the trigger element using `removeEventListener` so subsequent clicks no longer mutate state.

resource-hint-preloader.promptSeed:
Implement a dynamic resource hint injector that adds deduplicated `<link rel="preload">` and `<link rel="prefetch">` tags with priority hints to the document head:

## Description

Optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and route transitions often requires dynamically injecting `<link rel="preload">` or `<link rel="prefetch">` hints for hero images, fonts, or upcoming route chunks—while avoiding duplicate tags and setting `crossOrigin` and `fetchpriority` attributes properly.

```ts
interface ResourceHint {
  href: string;
  rel?: 'preload' | 'prefetch';
  as?: 'image' | 'script' | 'style' | 'font' | 'fetch';
  fetchPriority?: 'high' | 'low' | 'auto';
  crossOrigin?: 'anonymous' | 'use-credentials' | '';
}
```

### `preloadResources(resources: ResourceHint[], targetHead?: HTMLElement): HTMLLinkElement[]`

Injects `<link>` resource hint elements into `targetHead` (defaulting to `document.head`) and returns only the newly created `HTMLLinkElement` nodes:
- **Deduplication**:
  - Checks existing `<link>` elements inside `targetHead` as well as earlier items in the `resources` array.
  - Skips any entry where a `<link>` with the same `rel` (default `'preload'`) and `href` attribute already exists in `targetHead`.
- **Element Configuration**:
  - Sets `rel` (defaults to `'preload'`) and `href` attributes.
  - When `as` is provided, sets `link.as = as` (and `as` attribute).
  - When `fetchPriority` is provided, sets `link.setAttribute('fetchpriority', fetchPriority)`.
  - Sets `crossOrigin`: uses `resource.crossOrigin` if provided; otherwise, if `as === 'font'`, automatically sets `crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` (required by browsers for font preloads).
- **DOM Insertion**:
  - Appends each newly created `<link>` to `targetHead` in order and returns the array of newly inserted `HTMLLinkElement` elements.

xss-html-sanitizer.promptSeed:
Implement an allowlist-based HTML sanitizer using `DOMParser` to strip XSS vectors while preserving safe markup:

## Description

Rendering user-generated HTML with `innerHTML` or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` exposes applications to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via `<script>` tags, `<iframe>` embeds, inline `on*` event handlers, and `javascript:` URIs. Using `DOMParser` to parse untrusted markup into an inert document allows safe DOM-tree traversal and allowlist filtering.

### `sanitizeHtml(dirtyHtml: string): string`

Parses `dirtyHtml` with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(dirtyHtml, 'text/html')` and returns sanitized `body.innerHTML`:

> [!NOTE]
> `ALLOWED_TAGS: Set<string>` and `DROP_TAGS: Set<string>` (uppercase tag names) are preloaded in scope so you do not need to type out the tag lists:
> - `ALLOWED_TAGS`: `A`, `B`, `BLOCKQUOTE`, `BR`, `CODE`, `DIV`, `EM`, `H1`–`H6`, `I`, `LI`, `OL`, `P`, `PRE`, `SPAN`, `STRONG`, `UL`
> - `DROP_TAGS`: `SCRIPT`, `STYLE`, `IFRAME`, `OBJECT`, `EMBED`, `NOSCRIPT`, `TEMPLATE`, `SVG`, `MATH`

- **Element Filtering**:
  - Completely removes any element whose uppercase `tagName` is in `DROP_TAGS` (including its contents).
  - Preserves elements in `ALLOWED_TAGS`.
  - Unwraps any other non-allowlisted elements (replacing the element with its sanitized child nodes).
- **Attribute Filtering**:
  - Strips all `on*` event handler attributes (e.g., `onclick`, `onerror`, `onload`) and `style`.
  - Keeps only safe attributes: `title` and `class` on any allowlisted element, plus `href`, `target`, and `rel` on `<a>` elements.
- **URL Protocol Safety (`href`)**:
  - Strips control characters and whitespace when inspecting the scheme (catching obfuscated payloads like `java\nscript:`).
  - Allows only `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, or relative paths (`/`, `#`, `?`, or paths without a scheme).
  - Removes `href` if it uses `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:`, or any other disallowed scheme.
  - On `<a target="_blank">`, sets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
